Footnotes, endnotes & images What you're doing: adding the apparatus of a serious book — notes that link both ways, and pictures that sit in the text the way you placed them. Notes Place the cursor where the note belongs and use the Endnote toolbar button (or type a reference like [^1] ), then write the note's text where Beuk asks for it. In the preview, the reference is a small linked number. Tap it and you land on the note; the note carries a back-link that returns you to the exact line you left. In the exported EPUB these are true notes — marked with the proper epub:type semantics — so e-readers can offer them as pop-ups where they support it, and as a notes section where they don't. A reference with no note behind it degrades politely to a plain superscript number. It never becomes a dead link in a reader's hands. Images Use Insert Image in the editor. Upload a JPG or PNG to the book's image library, or pick one already there. Write the alt text. One plain sentence describing the image for readers who can't see it. Stores increasingly require it; readers have always deserved it. Choose Standard (sits within the text column) or Full-bleed (runs to the page edges where the reading system allows). Placed images can be adjusted later from the strip under the editor: change alt text, toggle full-bleed, or remove the placement (the library keeps the file). Typing the marks yourself Every button in the editor simply types a small mark for you. If you ever write or import text by hand, these are all of them — you never need this list to use Beuk; it's here for the curious. *** alone on a line — a scene break (it wears whichever ornament the book's typesetting chose). > at the start of a line — a blockquote. *italic* and **bold** — emphasis, the usual way. [^1] in the text, with its note defined on its own line as [^1]: the note itself — a linked endnote. An image sits on its own line, placed by Insert Image from the book's library. And one thing needs no mark at all: Auto-Format. Straight quotes become smart quotes, double hyphens become em-dashes, three dots become an ellipsis — the preview and the exported EPUB always use the polished text. What can go wrong My note appears twice / the numbering restarts. Notes are numbered per section, which is the convention stores expect. If a note looks duplicated, check you didn't also type its text into the body — the definition line itself never prints. An image is missing from the export. Run the validator — it lists every image in the package and flags any without alt text or a manifest entry. Full-bleed looks ordinary in the preview. In the device preview, full-bleed spans the full text column; true edge-to-edge breakout shows in the standalone HTML export and supporting readers. That's the honest state of e-reader support, not a fault in your file.
